🔥🇲🇽 <u>Regulator Fines Salinas Pliego's TV Azteca for Keeping Investors in the Dark</u>

Mexico's banking and securities commission, the CNBV, fined TV Azteca 2,688,600 pesos for withholding information from investors in 2021. That was the pandemic year when the network struggled to pay its dollar debt and issued 12 "relevant event" notices about swings in its share price and trading volume.

The fine was imposed on October 8 and only came to light through La Jornada. TV Azteca says it will challenge it. The $400 million in notes it set out to "reorganize" in 2021 is now being litigated in a New York federal court, and the company delisted from the Mexican stock exchange in March. The obligations from its years on the exchange still apply.
banner: TV AZTECA FINED 2.69M PESOS BY CNBV

🇲🇽📱 <u>Mexico Gets Google, Meta and TikTok to Co-Sign a Guide Against Digital Violence</u>

On 25N, Women's Secretary Laura Itzel Castillo presented a federal guide to digital rights and safety, produced with Google, Meta and TikTok under the agreement Mexico signed with the platforms on March 11, 2026.

It explains how to spot online harassment and threats, how to protect devices and personal data, the risks of AI-made abuse, and where to report. It has separate sections for girls, teenagers, parents, caregivers and older women. The platforms are now named in an official document on what they owe Mexican users.
banner: DIGITAL VIOLENCE: GUIDE WITH BIG TECH

text:
🔥🇲🇽 <u>Sheinbaum: The INE Could Have Broken the Ballot-Box Monopoly Itself</u>

Sheinbaum says the electoral institute never needed the antitrust authority to open its contracts for electoral materials. It writes its own bidding rules and chose rules that kept the same suppliers winning.

"If you've always hired one company and the next tender says 'only companies with experience may participate,' you've already rigged it, because the only one with experience is the one you hired the last three years." Her proposal: open every material to competition, and print ballots only at the state-owned Talleres Gráficos de México, with a custody chain from the press to the polling station.

🇲🇽☕ <u>Nestlé Blinks: Promises to Buy More Mexican Coffee, Above World Prices</u>

Hours after Sheinbaum said Nestlé "has to pay" Chiapas growers a fair price, the company issued a statement under the Plan México framework. It says its 2026-2027 purchase plan will keep green coffee prices, robusta and arabica, above the London and New York benchmarks, and buy a bigger volume than last year.

The Tapachula protest is why. Growers said Nestlé paid them 43 pesos a kilo for coffee that sells for 580 on supermarket shelves, and the company buys about a quarter of Mexico's entire harvest, mostly through middlemen.

🚨🇲🇽 <u>Mexico Sends Washington a Diplomatic Note Over Inés Gómez Mont</u>

ICE detained her in Florida on October 30. Mexico holds three arrest warrants against her for organized crime, money laundering and aggravated tax fraud, tied to a shell-invoice scheme. Washington still let her fly to Spain on her Spanish passport.

Sheinbaum confirmed a formal diplomatic note to the US, an extradition request already filed with Spain, and a complaint to Interpol, which quietly dropped the red notice on Gómez Mont and her husband Víctor Manuel Álvarez Puga in September. She tied it to reciprocity: Mexico hands over fugitives on request, while its own requests, including Ayotzinapa suspect José Ulises Bernabé García, whose file she gave Marco Rubio personally, are still waiting.
banner: GÓMEZ MONT: DIPLOMATIC NOTE TO US

text:
🇲🇽🏭 <u>INFLATION 3.96%: STILL INSIDE BANXICO'S RANGE</u>

INEGI: annual inflation hit 3.96% in the first half of November, per El Economista. The bump came from the seasonal end of summer electricity subsidies in 11 cities, which lifted power bills more than 20%.

Core prices actually fell 0.10% in the fortnight (3.68% annual), and goods dropped 0.25% during the Buen Fin. The headline rate is still within Banxico's 2–4% target band.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>SUPREME COURT SINKS ANOTHER ELEKTRA AMPARO</u>

Mexico's Supreme Court unanimously denied Salinas Pliego's Nueva Elektra an amparo against the customs processing fee. Elektra wanted to pay the flat 461.61-peso rate that importers covered by trade agreements pay, instead of 8 pesos per 1,000 pesos of goods' value.

Justice Giovanni Figueroa: the difference is "objective and reasonable," set by Mexico's treaty commitments. It's another lost bid by Mexico's loudest tax dodger to rewrite the rules for himself.
banner: ELEKTRA LOSES AGAIN AT SUPREME COURT

🇲🇽🌎 <u>FEMICIDES DOWN 5% AS 100 WOMEN'S CENTERS OPEN</u>

On 25N, Women's Secretary Laura Itzel Castillo reported that Mexico's daily average of femicides fell just over 5% from January to August 2026. "No figure can satisfy us. Every life counts."

The 100 Centros LIBRES planned for 2026 are already open in all 32 states and have served more than 650,000 women. Sheinbaum announced 500 more for 2027.

🔥🇲🇽 <u>USAID FILES PUT CÓRDOVA'S INE IN THE LOOP</u>

Nearly 300 USAID documents, now published by the US State Department, show Mexico's INE under Lorenzo Córdova inside a US-funded "disinformation" network, Contralínea reports.

A 2019 paper from IFES, a USAID-funded electoral NGO, praises INE as "the first electoral body in the world" with memoranda of understanding with Facebook, Twitter and Google, signed for the 2018 elections. Before leaving office in 2023, Córdova toured Washington and met with IFES, the NED, IRI and NDI.

He's now a member of the opposition party Somos.
banner: USAIDGATE: CÓRDOVA'S INE IN THE FILES

text:
🇲🇽🌎 <u>MEXICO POSTS $1.14B CURRENT ACCOUNT SURPLUS</u>

Banxico: Mexico closed Q3 2026 with a current account surplus of $1,142 million, 0.2% of GDP. That's up from $904 million a year earlier and the second straight quarter in the black.

The engine: $16.2 billion in secondary income, mostly remittances sent home by Mexican workers, which more than covered an $8.3 billion goods-and-services deficit.
